name: Monport GM Pro 30W Fiber
tagline: Integrated 30W fiber with one-touch autofocus: Monport's budget everyday marker
tldr: The GM Pro 30W is an integrated fiber marker with a 30W MAX source, one-touch autofocus, electric lift and a 150 × 150 mm field. Monport lists 10,000 mm/s, 0.08 mm maximum marking depth and M² below 1.5. At $1,999.99 on Monport's store in October 2026 it undercuts the split GT 30W by about $440. No colour marking: the source has a fixed pulse.
mainObjective: Everyday marking of tags, tools and tumblers with autofocus

priceRange.note: Official Monport store, Oct 2026: $1,999.99 machine only, $2,149.99 with rotary axis, $2,199.99 with LightBurn Pro

engraveExample.description: Filled logo on stainless steel plate

cutExample.description: Not a sheet cutter: thin metal only, in many passes

cannot: Clear glass or acrylic marking (needs UV or CO₂)
Parts larger than the 150 × 150 mm field without repositioning

pros: Autofocus and electric lift for $1,999.99, about $440 less than the split GT 30W (Monport store, Oct 2026)
Tight beam (M² below 1.5) for small text, serial numbers and QR codes
Package includes safety goggles, positioning bars and test aluminum sheets
cons: Q-switched MAX source with a fixed 80–120 ns pulse: no controlled colour marking
0.78 mJ pulse energy and 0.08 mm listed depth: slow for deep engraving
Heaviest tier of the line at 17.1 kg despite the lowest power with autofocus

faq.question: How deep can the GM Pro 30W engrave?
faq.answer: Monport lists a maximum marking depth of 0.08 mm per job setting, with 0.78 mJ of pulse energy; deeper relief comes from repeated passes. In our benchmark estimate, a filled 10 × 10 cm logo on stainless steel takes about 4–11 minutes depending on fill density.

faq.question: GM Pro 30W or GM Pro 50W?
faq.answer: The 30W ($1,999.99) covers marking, tags and light engraving. The 50W ($2,498) shares the field, chassis and autofocus but adds pulse energy (1.1 mJ vs 0.78 mJ) and a deeper listed mark (0.10 mm), which shortens deep logos and thin-metal cut-outs. For $500 more, the 50W is the better buy if engraving depth pays the bills.

faq.question: Does the GM Pro 30W need an enclosure?
faq.answer: It is an open galvo with a Class 4 invisible beam. Monport includes safety goggles; an enclosure (Monport sells one for integrated fibers) is strongly advised if other people or pets share the room.

standoutFeatures.title: Autofocus under $2,000
standoutFeatures.body: One-touch autofocus and an electric Z lift at $1,999.99 in October 2026: switching between a flat tag and a taller tool no longer means adjusting focus by hand.

standoutFeatures.title: Fine beam for detail
standoutFeatures.body: Monport lists M² below 1.5 for the 30W, the tightest of the two MAX sources in the line, which favours small text and dense QR codes over raw depth.

beginnerNotes: This profile is the 30W tier of the GM Pro, the default choice for everyday metal marking with autofocus. Compare the other tiers via the chips.
proTips: Start with Monport's material presets, then refine speed and frequency on test squares. Clean the F-theta lens regularly: residue from coated tumblers builds up quickly.

editorialDepth.advantages: The GM Pro 30W gives a small shop autofocus and a precise beam for the price of a basic manual fiber, which suits tags, tools and personalised tumblers well.
editorialDepth.limitations: No colour marking, modest depth per pass and a 150 × 150 mm field. The specs are Monport's; no independent review yet.
